message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $211 and am on Ventnor Avenue after paying $22 rent. I own the pink and orange sets plus Water Works and Marvin Gardens, but New York Avenue is mortgaged so I cannot build there. I need $110 to unmortgage it. Opponent p2 has $239 and a complete dark blue set with mortgaged Indiana and North Carolina.

Opponent p2 cannot build houses on the dark blue set yet. One house on each property costs $400, but they only have $239. They could mortgage their railroads to raise cash and build, which would be dangerous.

p3 has $697 and brown hotels. p4 has $1752 with light blue hotels and owns Ventnor Avenue, which I also hold. The yellow set is incomplete because Atlantic Avenue is unowned.

Mortgaging all my properties would raise $535, giving me $746 total cash. Unmortgaging New York Avenue costs $110, leaving only $101. That is too little to cover hotel rent of $550–$600. I will not unmortgage or build.

I will not mortgage early. I should not trade with p4 because that would help them complete their yellow set and pay for hotels. I will also avoid selling Marvin Gardens or the pink properties to p4, and I will not fund p2's dark blue houses. p3 previously rejected a $400 offer for Marvin, so I will not reoffer below $350. p2 is offering Indiana or North Carolina, but those incomplete reds are not worth the cash.

p2 cannot build houses on the dark blue set. Even one house each would cost $175 and $200, but p2 only has $239. Two houses would cost $800 total. p4 can afford one house on each property with their $1752, so they survive. The immediate danger is a light blue hotel rent of $550–$600, which would bankrupt me at $211 unless I mortgage.

I cannot mortgage now because the action state is POST_TURN. I will wait until I am actually hit by rent before mortgaging, since early mortgages cost 10% interest and lose rent income. I am also considering selling Water Works for $75, but p3 already owns Electric Company so that utility alone is not a strong trade.

Selling Water Works to p3 would give them a utility monopoly, which could backfire. I am now considering trading with p3 for Illinois, since I need cash to unmortgage New York Avenue and build houses on the orange set.

The greens are split three ways. I cannot easily complete that set. I am now weighing two paths: survive and hope p4 lands on dark blue or brown hotels, or find a trade that threatens p4 directly. Funding p2 to build their dark blue set would backfire, since those hotels would also bankrupt me.

I will end my turn. No trade is available that benefits me without also strengthening an opponent.

I will end my turn. I may send a brief public message warning against selling to Gemini, or stay silent.
